Sushi prices across DFW vary widely depending on the restaurant type, location, and quality of fish. Here's a realistic breakdown of what you can expect to spend:

Not all sushi is created equal. Here's what to look for when choosing where to eat:

- • Fish has sheen, no dull or brown spots
- • No strong "fishy" smell — fresh fish smells like the ocean
- • Rice is warm and well-seasoned, not cold or crunchy
- • Chef slices to order (not pre-made in a case)
- • Consistent 4+ star reviews on Google
- • Visible sushi bar where you can watch prep
- • Menu changes seasonally (fresh fish varies)
- • Staff can explain sourcing and preparation
- • Buffet sushi sitting out under heat lamps
- • Heavy sauces masking fish flavor
- • Menu with 200+ items (quality over quantity)
- • No visible sushi preparation area
- • Ask the chef what's freshest today
- • Start with nigiri to test fish quality
- • Order smaller portions of more variety
- • Try the lunch special for best value
Based on Google reviews and local food blogs, these are the most-ordered sushi rolls across DFW restaurants:

Fresh and flavorful—that's our promise. We receive fish deliveries multiple times per week. Our sushi chefs slice each piece to order. You can watch them work at our sushi bar.

Welcome to the world of sushi! Start with our California Roll or Shrimp Tempura Roll—they're mild and delicious. Salmon rolls are also crowd-pleasers. Our servers are happy to guide you through the menu.

Omakase means 'I'll leave it to you'—the chef chooses your courses. It's a wonderful way to experience sushi. At Jinbeh, ask about our chef's selection for a curated tasting experience. Learn more in our omakase dining guide .

Yes! We offer several vegetarian rolls including cucumber roll, avocado roll, and vegetable tempura roll. Just let your server know about any dietary needs. We're happy to accommodate.

Absolutely! Our sushi travels well for takeout. Order online or call us directly. For the freshest experience, we recommend dining in at our sushi bar—it's worth the trip.

Sushi prices in Dallas range from $8-15 for basic rolls at casual spots to $100-200+ per person for omakase experiences. At Jinbeh, specialty rolls run $12-18 and lunch combos start around $12-15, offering excellent value for fresh, chef-prepared sushi.

The FDA advises pregnant women to avoid raw fish. At Jinbeh, cooked sushi options like shrimp tempura rolls, California rolls (which use imitation crab), and vegetable rolls are safe alternatives. Ask your server for fully-cooked options — there are plenty of delicious choices.

Sushi includes vinegared rice with various toppings or fillings (rolls, nigiri), while sashimi is thinly sliced raw fish served without rice. Both are available at Jinbeh. For a deep dive, check out our sashimi vs sushi guide .

Planning a birthday celebration? The right restaurant can transform an ordinary dinner into an unforgettable memory. When choosing where to celebrate, look for restaurants that offer something extra—complimentary desserts, entertainment, special songs, and experiences that go beyond ordinary meals.

"Your birthday deserves more than just good food. It deserves an experience that celebrates YOU. Whether you want an interactive hibachi show or an intimate dinner, we're here to make your special day unforgettable."

Did You Know?

Birthday dining is a $4.3 billion annual market in the US. Restaurants that offer interactive entertainment like hibachi shows see 3x higher birthday booking rates than traditional restaurants. The average birthday dinner group spends 40% more per person than regular diners, making birthdays the most profitable celebration type for restaurants.

Source: National Restaurant Association

Jinbeh is a fantastic choice if you're looking for a hibachi show that will dazzle your guests. Known for its theatrical cooking style, Jinbeh offers a fun and interactive dining experience. The skilled chefs not only prepare your meal in front of you but also put on a show with their knife skills and fiery tricks. For birthdays, Jinbeh often provides a complimentary dessert and a special birthday song. Learn more about planning the perfect hibachi birthday party . The interactive nature of the dining experience ensures that both you and your guests are entertained throughout the meal.

Beyond the entertainment, Jinbeh provides a communal atmosphere that is perfect for group celebrations. The shared tables and lively environment encourage interaction among guests, making it easy for everyone to join in the fun. Whether you're a regular or a first-time visitor, the staff at Jinbeh go above and beyond to ensure your birthday is celebrated with flair and excitement.

The Cheesecake Factory is renowned for its extensive menu and delectable cheesecakes. On your birthday, the restaurant takes it up a notch by offering a complimentary scoop of ice cream with a candle. It's a simple yet sweet gesture that makes your dining experience more enjoyable. Plus, with locations all over, finding a Cheesecake Factory "near me" is often easy, making it a convenient choice for birthday celebrations. For something more unique with entertainment, consider trying the best hibachi in Dallas instead.

In addition to the birthday perks, The Cheesecake Factory is known for its welcoming atmosphere and attentive service. The staff is trained to cater to special occasions, ensuring that your birthday is celebrated with the attention it deserves. The restaurant's vibrant ambiance and diverse menu make it a versatile choice for any type of birthday celebration.

Famous for its Italian-American cuisine, Olive Garden provides a warm and welcoming atmosphere perfect for family gatherings. For birthdays, the restaurant offers a complimentary dessert and sometimes the staff will sing you a birthday song. It's an ideal spot for those looking for food places for birthday celebrations that are both comfortable and festive.

Olive Garden's commitment to hospitality is evident in its birthday offerings. The complimentary dessert and birthday song are thoughtful touches that enhance the celebratory mood. The restaurant's focus on creating a family-friendly atmosphere ensures that guests of all ages feel welcome and appreciated.

If you're searching for a unique and adventurous dining experience, Rainforest Cafe is the place to be. With its jungle-themed decor and animatronic animals, it feels like dining in the heart of the rainforest. For birthdays, the restaurant offers a special birthday treat and a fun song, making it an exciting choice for kids and adults alike.

For those who enjoy a bit of history and theatrics, Medieval Times provides an unforgettable experience. This dinner theater offers a medieval-themed show complete with knights, horses, and jousting. On your birthday, you'll receive a special shout-out, making it a memorable event. It's perfect for anyone looking for places to eat on your birthday that also provide entertainment.

Known for its rock and roll theme, Hard Rock Cafe is a great place to celebrate a birthday with music lovers. The lively atmosphere, delicious food, and extensive collection of music memorabilia make it a standout choice. For birthdays, Hard Rock Cafe often provides a special dessert and a souvenir photo to commemorate your visit.

Many local steakhouses offer birthday specials that include complimentary appetizers or desserts. These local gems often provide a more intimate setting, perfect for a cozy birthday dinner. Be sure to check your favorite steakhouse "near me" to see what birthday specials they offer. The combination of delicious food, attentive service, and personalized birthday offerings makes local steakhouses a popular choice.

Family-owned Italian restaurants are known for their warm hospitality and delicious homemade dishes. Many of these restaurants offer a complimentary dessert or a glass of wine for birthdays, adding a personal touch to your celebration. It's a wonderful option for those looking for where to eat on your birthday with a homey feel.

Before deciding on a restaurant, call ahead or check their website to see what birthday specials they offer. Some restaurants require you to sign up for their rewards program to receive birthday perks. At Jinbeh, make a reservation to secure your special celebration.

Think about the kind of atmosphere you want for your birthday. Whether you prefer a lively, entertaining environment or a quiet, intimate setting, choose accordingly.

Popular restaurants can fill up quickly, especially on weekends. Book your table in advance to ensure you get a spot on your special day.

Reading reviews can give you a better idea of what to expect. Look for comments about the birthday experience to make an informed decision.

### Body content

Planning a bridal shower? Discover the best venues nearby—from intimate gardens and elegant hotels to charming cafes and unique event spaces perfect for celebrating the bride-to-be.

- Home
- Blog
- Bridal Shower Venues
Planning a bridal shower is an exciting yet important task. Finding the perfect venue is key to creating a memorable event that celebrates the bride-to-be in style. Whether you're looking for something traditional or a unique location that reflects the bride's personality, there are plenty of options to explore.

This guide helps you find the best bridal shower venues near you, from intimate gardens and elegant hotels to charming cafes and unique event spaces. Let's explore options that will make the bride-to-be feel cherished and celebrated.

Gardens offer picturesque backdrops perfect for bridal showers. The beauty of blooming flowers and the serenity of nature make events feel special. Look for botanical gardens or local parks with rentable spaces, including gazebos or pavilions reserved for private events.

These venues are ideal for outdoor celebrations and provide stunning photography opportunities. When planning an outdoor event, always check the weather forecast and have a rain backup plan. Many botanical gardens are in high demand during peak blooming seasons, so book well in advance.

For a touch of culture and sophistication, consider hosting a bridal shower in an art gallery or museum. These venues provide unique ambiance with stunning visuals and an artistic atmosphere. The existing artwork adds to the event's elegance without requiring extensive decoration.

Many galleries and museums have event spaces available for rent, making them ideal for intimate gatherings. The cultural backdrop makes conversations flow naturally and provides beautiful photo opportunities that capture the bride's sophisticated taste.

Cafes and tea rooms are perfect for smaller, more intimate bridal showers. They provide cozy settings ideal for close friends and family gatherings. Look for venues offering afternoon tea service or customizable menu options to add personal touches to your celebration.

The relaxed, welcoming atmosphere of cafes encourages conversation and connection. Many offer beautiful decor and ambiance that requires minimal additional decoration. Tea service adds an elegant, refined quality to the event.

If you prefer a personal, intimate setting, consider hosting at someone's home or renting an Airbnb. This option allows complete customization and flexibility. You can decorate the space to match the bride's style and maintain full control over the guest list and activities.

Home-based showers create a warm, welcoming atmosphere and allow guests to relax and feel truly at home. This option is ideal for groups of 15-40 guests and can be very budget-friendly while still feeling elegant and special.

"Hosting our bridal shower at Jinbeh was perfect. The elegant setting, beautiful private space, and attentive service made the bride feel so special and celebrated."

— Bridal Shower Host

Did You Know?

The bridal shower industry is worth $2.8 billion annually in the US. Restaurant-hosted bridal showers have surged 55% since 2020, with 68% of maid-of-honor hosts preferring venues that handle food and service. The average bridal shower costs $2,500-$5,000, with venue and catering being the largest expenses at 40-50% of the total budget.

Source: The Knot & WeddingWire

Restaurants like Jinbeh in Frisco and Lewisville offer excellent bridal shower options. Private dining spaces provide intimate, elegant atmospheres without requiring extensive decoration. You can customize menus to accommodate guest preferences and dietary needs. We also offer catering services for flexible options.

Professional restaurant staff handles all service logistics, allowing you to focus on celebrating. Beautiful ambiance and attention to detail make guests feel valued. Restaurants often provide packages that include beverages, special presentations, and personalized service.

For larger bridal showers, banquet halls are classic choices. These venues offer ample space and often provide catering and decoration services. They're well-equipped to handle bigger groups and can be customized to fit any theme or color scheme.

Banquet halls typically offer flexible room configurations, professional setup support, and often include audio-visual equipment for presentations or slideshows. They're ideal for showers with 50+ guests and provide reliable, professional environments.

Hotels and resorts are excellent for larger gatherings. Many feature beautiful ballrooms or event spaces that can be transformed to match your vision. They often offer comprehensive packages including catering, decoration, and accommodation for out-of-town guests.

Hotels provide professional event coordination, convenient on-site amenities, and sophisticated settings that make guests feel special. Multi-day celebrations can be arranged with hotel stays. They're ideal for showers with 75+ guests.

Wineries and breweries offer relaxed, fun atmospheres perfect for bridal showers. These venues often have tasting rooms or private event spaces ideal for celebrating. Guests can enjoy wine or craft beer selections, adding a unique, sophisticated twist to traditional shower concepts.

The casual-yet-elegant vibe appeals to modern brides. These venues often provide food pairings with beverages, creating memorable culinary experiences. They work well for groups of 20-80 guests.

Barn venues provide charming, rustic vibes perfect for country-themed showers. Many barns maintain rustic charm while offering modern amenities, creating unique, down-to-earth settings for celebration.

These venues are popular for outdoor ceremony setups and provide plenty of space for activities and dancing. Barn events often feel more relaxed and personal while still maintaining elegance and style.

When selecting a venue, consider its location and accessibility for all guests. Ensure ample parking or easy public transportation access. The venue should be convenient for most guests, especially if you have attendees traveling from out of town. Jinbeh offers convenient locations with ample parking in both our Frisco and Lewisville areas.

Ensure the venue comfortably accommodates your guest list. Check what amenities are included—tables, chairs, audio-visual equipment. Some venues offer additional services like catering, decoration, or event coordination, which simplify planning significantly.

Set a realistic budget for the venue and stick to it. Bridal showers range from simple gatherings to extravagant events. Choose a venue fitting your financial plan. Don't forget additional costs like food, decorations, and entertainment.

Most importantly, consider the bride's tastes and personality. Does she prefer intimate gatherings or larger celebrations? Modern elegance or rustic charm? The best venue reflects her style and makes her feel cherished.

- Visit venues in person before booking to assess ambiance and suitability
- Book early for desired dates, especially during peak seasons
- Confirm inclusions such as tables, chairs, parking, and amenities
- Discuss menu options and dietary accommodations
- Get cancellation policies in writing
- Ask about setup and cleanup assistance
Finding the perfect venue for a bridal shower involves considering the bride's tastes and guest needs. Whether you choose a small, intimate gathering or a larger celebration, countless options suit any preference. From charming gardens to elegant hotels and unique event spaces, the perfect bridal shower venue awaits.

At Jinbeh, we specialize in creating memorable celebrations. Our private dining spaces provide elegant, intimate atmospheres perfect for bridal showers. Our professional team handles logistics while you focus on celebrating the bride-to-be. We also offer catering services for off-site events.

By taking time to explore your options and plan carefully, you'll create a memorable event that the bride will cherish forever. Consider a Jinbeh gift card as a shower gift the bride-to-be can enjoy anytime. Whether you choose an intimate garden gathering, elegant hotel ballroom, or unique specialty venue, the key is selecting a space that reflects the bride's personality and makes her feel celebrated and loved.

For an interactive celebration with beautiful ambiance, visit our Frisco location or Lewisville location to host your bridal shower at Jinbeh.

Happy planning, and here's to a wonderful bridal shower celebration!

### Body content

Explore Japanese beverages from premium sake and Yamazaki whiskey to signature cocktails and Ramune soda. Your complete guide to drinks at Jinbeh in Frisco & Lewisville, TX.

Japanese culture has produced some of the world's most refined beverages — from the ancient art of sake brewing to the modern mastery of Japanese whiskey. At Jinbeh, our bar showcases the best of these traditions alongside creative signature cocktails. Explore our beverage guides to learn, taste, and discover your new favorite drink.

Explore our curated collection of guides, tips, and recommendations.

Expert tips for pairing sake with sushi, hibachi, and appetizers.

Junmai, Daiginjo, Nigori — learn the sake family.

Find your perfect sake: dry, sweet, fruity, or rich.

How strong is sake compared to wine, beer, and spirits?

Creative Japanese-inspired cocktails from our bar.

From matcha to Ramune — every Japanese drink you should try.

Why the world is obsessed with Japanese whiskey.

Deep dive into Suntory's legendary Yamazaki single malt.

The iconic marble-sealed Japanese soda — flavors and how to open it.

Common questions about japanese beverages at Jinbeh.

Sake is a Japanese rice wine made by fermenting polished rice with water, yeast, and koji mold. The more the rice is polished, the higher the grade — Daiginjo sake uses rice polished to at least 50% of its original size.

Jinbeh's bar features a curated selection of Japanese whiskeys including Suntory Yamazaki, Hibiki Harmony, Toki, and Nikka Coffey Grain. Ask your bartender for a whiskey flight or a Japanese highball.

Ramune is a beloved Japanese carbonated soft drink known for its unique marble-sealed glass bottle. It comes in dozens of flavors including original, strawberry, melon, and lychee. We serve Ramune at both Jinbeh locations — kids and adults love it!

Join us for unforgettable hibachi performances and fresh sushi. Family-owned since 1988, two convenient locations in Frisco and Lewisville.

Dive deep into Japanese cuisine — from the art of sushi and sashimi to teppanyaki grilling and traditional dishes. Expert guides from Jinbeh's 38+ years of culinary heritage.

Japanese cuisine is one of the world's great culinary traditions, built on principles of freshness, seasonality, and presentation. At Jinbeh, we honor these traditions while making them accessible to every guest. Whether you're curious about the difference between sashimi and sushi or want to master chopstick etiquette, these guides draw from our 38+ years of serving authentic Japanese food in North Texas.

Explore our curated collection of guides, tips, and recommendations.

Every sushi style explained — nigiri, maki, temaki, and more.

What's the real difference between sashimi and sushi?

Etiquette, chopstick tips, and wasabi guidelines.

The surprising difference between these two cooking styles.

Visual guide to identifying sushi by type.

How Japanese food culture shapes the dining experience.

Exploring the diverse Asian food scene in Dallas.

Common questions about japanese cuisine guide at Jinbeh.

Jinbeh serves authentic Japanese cuisine including sushi, sashimi, hibachi (teppanyaki), tempura, teriyaki, udon, and Japanese appetizers. We also offer a full bar with sake, Japanese whiskey, and signature cocktails.

Omakase means 'I'll leave it to you' in Japanese. It's a dining style where the chef selects and prepares a multi-course meal based on the freshest ingredients available. At Jinbeh, our sushi chefs craft a personalized omakase experience at the sushi bar.

Japanese cuisine is widely regarded as one of the healthiest in the world. It emphasizes fresh fish, vegetables, rice, and minimal use of heavy oils. Sashimi, edamame, and grilled hibachi proteins are all nutritious options at Jinbeh.

Join us for unforgettable hibachi performances and fresh sushi. Family-owned since 1988, two convenient locations in Frisco and Lewisville.

Discover the health benefits of Japanese food. Calorie guides for hibachi and sushi, nutritious menu options, and how Japanese dining fits a healthy lifestyle.

Japanese cuisine is celebrated worldwide for its health benefits — and for good reason. With an emphasis on fresh fish, vegetables, lean proteins, and minimal processing, a meal at Jinbeh can be both delicious and nutritious. These guides break down the calories, nutrition facts, and healthiest choices on our menu.

Explore our curated collection of guides, tips, and recommendations.

Calorie counts for popular hibachi dishes and healthier swaps.

Quick, balanced hibachi lunches for weekday dining.

Affordable lunch combos with fresh sushi rolls.

Which is healthier? Comparing nutrition of sashimi and sushi.

Omega-3 rich salmon sashimi — one of the healthiest menu picks.

Common questions about health & nutrition at Jinbeh.

A typical hibachi entree at Jinbeh ranges from 400–800 calories depending on your protein choice and sides. Chicken is the lightest option (~450 cal), while steak and shrimp combo plates are around 650–800 calories. Hibachi vegetables and salad add minimal calories.

Yes! Sushi is one of the healthiest dining options. A typical sushi roll has 200–350 calories and is rich in omega-3 fatty acids, lean protein, and vitamins. Sashimi (pure sliced fish) is even lower in calories while being packed with protein.

Our healthiest dishes include sashimi platters, edamame, miso soup, grilled salmon, chicken hibachi with vegetables, and low-sodium sushi rolls. Ask your server about lighter preparation options — we're happy to accommodate dietary preferences.

Join us for unforgettable hibachi performances and fresh sushi. Family-owned since 1988, two convenient locations in Frisco and Lewisville.

Teppanyaki (鉄板焼き) means "grilling on an iron plate." It's the art form behind what Americans call "hibachi restaurants"—where skilled chefs transform cooking into dinner theater.

See also: popular Japanese culture

"At Jinbeh, our teppanyaki chefs train for years to perfect their craft. It's not just about the food—it's about creating unforgettable moments around the grill."

Did You Know?

Teppanyaki was invented in 1945 at a restaurant called Misono in Kobe, Japan — specifically to appeal to Western visitors. The communal flat-griddle format was designed so foreign diners could watch their food being prepared, building trust in unfamiliar cuisine.

Source: Japanese Culinary History

Precision cuts, rapid chopping

Onion volcano, flaming shrimp

Catch the shrimp in your mouth!

### Body content

Japanese dining doesn't have to mean a long sit-down meal. At Jinbeh, you can enjoy authentic sushi, bento boxes, and hibachi lunches at your own pace—from a quick 30-minute lunch to a full evening experience.

Key Takeaway

At Jinbeh, 'fast casual' doesn't mean cutting corners. Whether you have 30 minutes for a sushi lunch or a full evening for hibachi, we deliver the same quality and care that has kept us going for over 38 years.

- Home
- Blog
- Fast Casual Dining Jinbeh
"Fast casual" and "Japanese restaurant" might seem like a n unusual combination. After all, Japanese cuisine is known for precision, artistry, and presentation—things that take time. But at Jinbeh , we've spent 38 years learning how to deliver quality at every speed.

Jinbeh's menu philosophy emerged from decades of trial and error. The original Las Colinas menu was a thick book of truly authentic Japanese dishes — like salted mackerel and traditional set menus. Over time, they learned: people want American authentic . Food that feels genuinely Japanese enough to transport you, but not so foreign that you're uncomfortable. “We chose a different path: family-friendly, accessible, and large enough to serve the community.”

D Magazine has recognized Jinbeh multiple times across their Best of Big D and Best Neighborhood Restaurants franchises. That kind of sustained editorial recognition — spanning the original Las Colinas location through today's Frisco and Lewisville restaurants — speaks to consistency that most restaurants never achieve.

Need a quick lunch? Our sushi bar serves fresh rolls in minutes. Planning a special date night ? Settle in for a full hibachi experience. The choice is yours—and the quality never changes.

Did You Know?

The fast casual dining segment has grown into a $263 billion industry in the US, growing 10% annually — faster than any other restaurant category. While most fast casual spots sacrifice quality for speed, family-owned restaurants like Jinbeh prove you can have both: fresh, made-to-order Japanese cuisine served at your pace, whether that's a 30-minute sushi lunch or a full evening hibachi experience.

Source: National Restaurant Association 2025 Industry Report

Our most popular fast casual lunch picks:

Pull up a seat at the sushi bar and watch our chefs work while your order is prepared. For the sushi curious , this is the best seat in the house—ask your chef for recommendations. Most rolls are ready in 5-10 minutes.

Our bento boxes are the ultimate work lunch: a balanced combination of protein, rice, salad, and sides in one convenient box. Choose from chicken teriyaki, salmon, shrimp, or a vegetarian option . Each box is a complete meal that's satisfying without being heavy.

Our hibachi lunch specials offer the same tableside cooking experience at a great value. You'll get miso soup, house salad, your choice of grilled protein, fried rice, and vegetables. It takes a little longer than the sushi bar (about 45-60 minutes with the show), but it's worth every minute.

A lot of "fast casual" Japanese spots have popped up across DFW—many of them serving pre-made sushi from a case or reheated teriyaki from a steam table. We take a different approach:

- Everything made to order — No pre-rolled sushi sitting in a display case
- Fresh fish daily — We source quality ingredients, not shortcuts
- Skilled chefs, not assembly lines — Our sushi and hibachi chefs are trained professionals
- Real hospitality — Guests say our service is "friendly and professional"
- Family-owned since 1988 — We care because it's personal
As one reviewer put it: "The food is tasty and enjoyable—you can tell the difference between Jinbeh and the quick-serve Japanese places." That's the difference 38 years of experience makes.

- 30-minute lunch break? → Sushi bar or bento box pickup
- Working lunch with clients? → Private dining room with pre-ordered menu
- Weeknight dinner? → Full hibachi experience
- Special celebration? → Birthday hibachi with the full show
- No time to dine in? → Takeout or delivery
Insider Tip

Visit us for lunch Monday through Friday and discover why Jinbeh is the best of both worlds: restaurant-quality Japanese food that works with your schedule. Check our full menu and see what catches your eye.

Lunch at the sushi bar is typically 30-40 minutes. Hibachi lunch takes about 45-60 minutes including the chef performance. If you're in a hurry, call ahead and we can have your order ready for pickup in 20-30 minutes.

Yes! We offer lunch combinations that include your choice of protein with miso soup, house salad, rice, and grilled vegetables—all at an excellent value compared to dinner pricing. Check our menu page or call for current lunch specials.

Fast casual Japanese focuses on quick service, affordable prices, and efficient ordering—think sushi counters and ramen shops. Fine dining emphasizes the full experience: ambiance, presentation, and service. Jinbeh bridges both worlds with a warm, family-run atmosphere that delivers quality food quickly when needed.

Absolutely! Order a bento box, sushi roll combo, or chicken teriyaki for a satisfying work lunch. Call ahead for pickup from Frisco (214) 619-1200 or Lewisville (214) 488-2224, and your order will be ready in 20-30 minutes. You can also order through Grubhub or Uber Eats.

Yes! You can order through delivery apps like DoorDash, Uber Eats, and Grubhub for both pickup and delivery. Ten years ago, "fine dining in Frisco" meant driving to Dallas. Not anymore. Frisco has quietly built one of the most exciting upscale restaurant scenes in North Texas—and the best spots aren't always the ones with the biggest marketing budgets.

"Fine dining isn't just about exceptional food—it's about creating memories through an unforgettable experience. At Jinbeh, we combine authentic Japanese tradition with contemporary elegance, delivering culinary artistry in every dish."

Did You Know?

Frisco's population has exploded from just 33,000 in 2000 to over 230,000 today, making it one of the fastest-growing cities in America. This growth has attracted over 500 restaurants to the area — but Jinbeh has been a Frisco dining institution since 1988, predating most of the city's modern development by over a decade.

Source: U.S. Census Bureau & City of Frisco

Frisco's explosive growth has attracted top culinary talent from across the region. The city's commitment to quality living extends to its dining scene, where restaurants prioritize fresh ingredients, innovative techniques, and exceptional service. Whether you're a local or visiting, you'll find that Frisco's fine dining establishments rival those in Dallas's most prestigious neighborhoods.

Japanese and international restaurants honor time-tested culinary techniques

Classically trained professionals with decades of experience

Daily sourcing of fresh, high-quality produce and proteins

Sophisticated settings that enhance the dining experience

When it comes to fine dining in Frisco, Jinbeh stands as a cornerstone of excellence. This renowned Japanese restaurant has built its reputation over decades by combining authentic Japanese culinary traditions with a sophisticated, welcoming atmosphere. The moment you step through Jinbeh's doors, you're transported to a realm where quality reigns supreme.

Jinbeh's hibachi experience is far more than just a meal—it's a performance. Skilled chefs orchestrate a spectacular show, preparing your meal with precision and flair directly before your eyes. The sizzling sounds, tantalizing aromas, and expertly executed techniques create an atmosphere that's as entertaining as it is delicious.

The hibachi chicken, steak, and seafood at Jinbeh are cooked to perfection, ensuring that flavors are locked in and textures are just right. Diners are treated to culinary tricks like shrimp flips into chef's hats and signature onion volcanoes—a true feast for the senses.

For steak enthusiasts, Jinbeh offers a revelation. Each steak is sourced from premium cuts and cooked to your exact preference. The combination of expert cooking technique and carefully selected accompaniments—from wasabi-infused butter to soy-ginger glaze—creates a dining experience that's both sophisticated and unforgettable.

No fine dining experience is complete without the perfect libation. Jinbeh's mixologists at our bar craft sophisticated cocktails using fresh ingredients and premium spirits. The restaurant's curated sake recommendations complement its Japanese cuisine beautifully, with options ranging from traditional varieties to innovative creations featuring exotic fruits and contemporary flavor profiles.

Jinbeh has been a cornerstone of Frisco's dining scene since 1988. We've earned a top-rated Google rating through unwavering commitment to quality, authenticity, and hospitality.

Every plate is a work of art. At Jinbeh, the presentation of sushi, hibachi dishes, and cocktails reflects the restaurant's commitment to culinary excellence and aesthetic refinement.

Whether you're celebrating an anniversary , hosting a corporate event, or marking a milestone birthday, fine dining restaurants in Frisco—especially Jinbeh—can customize the experience to your preferences.

Red Robin offers a free birthday burger to Red Robin Royalty Program members. Simply sign up before your birthday, and you're eligible for a complimentary gourmet burger. Red Robin is renowned for diverse gourmet burgers, each crafted with unique flavors and quality ingredients.

Fire shoots up from the onion volcano. The whole table gasps, then laughs. The birthday kid's eyes go wide as the chef flips a shrimp toward their plate. This is why hibachi makes birthdays unforgettable.

Jinbeh's birthday celebrations follow a precise system: (1) The host identifies the birthday person on arrival and says happy birthday. (2) The server is notified and acknowledges the celebration. (3) The chef joins in for the grand finale — ice cream with tambourines and noisemakers. Every child also receives a hand-folded origami crane from a basket at the host stand. This isn't scripted corporate friendliness — it's genuine family warmth practiced since 1988.

Every birthday at Jinbeh follows our signature three-touch system, developed over 38 years of celebrating with families:

- The Host — First to acknowledge. When checking in, the host identifies the birthday person and personally says happy birthday.
- The Server — Notified by the host. The birthday person's seat is circled on the order sheet.
- The Chef — Informed that there's a birthday at the table.
The finale: front-of-house staff arrives with ice cream, tambourines, and noisemakers. And every child leaves with a hand-folded origami crane from a basket by the door.

We've hosted thousands of birthday celebrations at Jinbeh since 1988. From 5-year-olds mesmerized by flames to 50th birthday bashes with sake toasts, we've seen what makes hibachi parties work—and what can go wrong without proper planning. Not sure what to give the birthday person? A Jinbeh gift card is always the perfect present.

This guide shares everything we've learned about throwing the perfect hibachi birthday party.

Most restaurants offer food. Hibachi offers an experience. When you book a birthday at a hibachi vs teppanyaki experience , you're not just choosing a menu—you're choosing entertainment that brings everyone together.

No need to hire a clown or plan activities. Your chef IS the entertainment. For an hour or more, guests watch a skilled performer juggle spatulas, create fire volcanos, and turn dinner into a show. Even the most reserved guests end up cheering when the chef catches an egg in his hat.

"It's truly the perfect place for kids, birthdays, and entertaining the whole fam! The chefs are very entertaining. They always put on an excellent show!"

— Jinbeh Guest Review

Did You Know?

Americans spend over $12 billion dining out for birthday celebrations each year, making it the #1 reason people eat at restaurants outside of regular meals. Hibachi/teppanyaki restaurants see a 40% increase in bookings during birthday season (May-August), and the interactive chef performance eliminates the need for separate entertainment — saving the average party host $200-$500 on entertainment costs.

Source: National Restaurant Association & Event Planning Institute

At most restaurants, food arrives at different times. Uncle Jim finishes his steak while Grandma's salad hasn't arrived. At hibachi, everyone's meal is prepared and served together. The birthday person isn't eating alone while others wait.

A 7-year-old's eyes light up watching flames dance. A 70-year-old appreciates the theatrical knife skills. Hibachi bridges generations in a way few dining experiences can. We regularly host parties where the youngest guest is 3 and the oldest is 83. Looking for dining venues suitable for group dining ? Hibachi is ideal for any gathering.

Weekend dinner slots (Friday 6-8pm, Saturday 5-8pm) book fastest. If your schedule allows flexibility, consider:

- Sunday lunch: Less crowded, more attention from staff, and often easier to get your whole group seated together
- Weeknight dinner: Tuesday through Thursday gives you a more intimate experience without the weekend rush
- Lunch parties: Same great show, lower prices, perfect for kids' parties that don't run too late
Call the restaurant directly—don't just book online. Tell them:

- It's a birthday celebration
- Your exact party size (don't estimate—count heads)
- Age of the birthday person (helps chef calibrate the show)
- Any dietary restrictions or allergies
- If you want the group seated together at one grill—for large parties, ask about our private dining options
At Jinbeh, our Frisco location and Lewisville location both accommodate groups of various sizes. Call us at (214) 619-1200 (Frisco) or (214) 488-2224 (Lewisville) to discuss your party needs.

Hibachi dining has its own rhythm. Let guests know:

- Arrive on time. If the rest of the table starts without you, you'll miss part of the show.
- Expect communal seating. You might share a grill with non-party guests if your group doesn't fill the table.
- Plan for 90 minutes to 2 hours. Hibachi isn't fast casual—the experience takes time.
- Come hungry. Portions are generous. "Large portions all around and food left to take home," as our regulars say.
Kids go absolutely wild for hibachi. The flames, the tricks, the catching-food-in-your-mouth games—it's interactive in a way tablets and movies can't match.

Pro tips for kids' parties:

- Book a lunch slot—kids have more energy earlier, and you'll have the restaurant more to yourselves
- Tell the chef it's a kids' party so they can emphasize the playful tricks over the technical skills
- Consider the chicken and shrimp combo—it's universally kid-friendly
- Bring your own cake or cupcakes—most hibachi restaurants allow this (confirm when booking)
See our kids birthday packages →

Teens can be tough to impress, but hibachi gets them off their phones. The spectacle is Instagram-worthy (the flames, the food artistry), and the communal experience forces actual conversation.

Pro tips for teen parties:

- Let them choose their own entrees—teens appreciate autonomy
- A dinner time slot feels more "grown up" than lunch
- Encourage photos and videos of the chef show—it's content gold
For adults, hibachi offers the rare combination of great food, entertainment, and an atmosphere that encourages conversation. It's sophisticated enough for milestone birthdays but fun enough that nobody feels stuffy.

Pro tips for adult parties:

- Start with sake recommendations at the bar before your table is ready
- Order family-style types of sushi as an appetizer for the table to share
- Filet mignon and lobster are premium options that feel celebratory
- Take advantage of happy hour specials if timing works
Hibachi menus can feel overwhelming if you've never been. Here's what sells most for birthday parties:

- Hibachi Filet Mignon: The celebratory choice. Tender, flavorful, and feels special.
- Hibachi Shrimp & Chicken Combo: Best of both worlds, perfect for the indecisive.
- Hibachi Salmon: A lighter option that still delivers on flavor.
- Vegetable Hibachi: Don't overlook this—the mushrooms, zucchini, and onions cooked hibachi-style are incredible.
- Extra lobster tail: Splits nicely if the birthday person wants to taste everything
- Gyoza (dumplings): Perfect appetizer for passing around
- Sushi platter: A showstopping centerpiece before the hibachi begins. Learn more about how to order sushi if your guests are new to Japanese dining.
Let's talk real numbers. Here's what to expect:

"Oh, a few people might not make it." Then everyone shows up, and you're scrambling. Book for your actual headcount—it's easier to release seats than add them.

Hibachi timing is precise. If your reservation is 6:30, the chef starts cooking at 6:30. Arrive 10-15 minutes early to order drinks, settle in, and be ready when the show begins.

Don't surprise the restaurant. When you call ahead and mention it's a birthday, we can seat you at a grill with the best view, give your chef a heads up, and make sure the birthday person feels celebrated.

Saturday at 7pm is the busiest slot. The restaurant is packed, wait times are longer, and your party might feel rushed. Friday evening or Sunday afternoon gives you a better experience with the same great food.

Learn the calorie content of Jinbeh hibachi dishes and make informed dietary choices. Discover healthy options that fit your lifestyle without sacrificing flavor.

Key Takeaway

Hibachi protein calories range from 150 cal (shrimp) to 450 cal (steak). Swap fried rice for steamed rice to save ~200 calories, load up on vegetables (50–70 cal), and request sauces on the side. A lean hibachi meal can total just 350–400 calories.

- Home
- Blog
- Hibachi Calories Guide
You love dining out. The social experience, the exceptional food, the entertainment. But you're also conscious about what you eat and how it fits into your health goals. Good news: you don't have to choose between these priorities.

Here's a nutrition secret from Jinbeh's kitchen: the fried rice actually contains finely chopped scallion, onion, and carrots — but they're cut so small you can't see them. This is deliberate. The restaurant learned early on that customers (especially kids) don't want visible vegetables in their rice. The chopping technique is so refined that the nutrition is there without the visual “objection.”

Understanding the nutritional content of your favorite dishes is the key to enjoying restaurant meals mindfully. At Jinbeh, our hibachi vs teppanyaki cooking methods are naturally well-suited to health-conscious dining. High-temperature grilling requires minimal added fats, ingredients are fresh and visible, and you control portion sizes and sauces.

This guide breaks down the calories and nutritional content of popular Jinbeh hibachi dishes, explains the health benefits of different proteins and sides, and provides practical strategies for enjoying the hibachi dining experience while meeting your dietary goals.

Unlike many restaurant preparation methods that rely on oil, butter, or heavy creams, hibachi cooking has several nutritional advantages:

Hibachi grills operate at high temperatures (around 400°F). This intense heat cooks proteins and vegetables quickly with minimal added oil. The food develops delicious caramelization and flavors without heavy sauces or butter-heavy cooking.

Unlike a hidden kitchen, your hibachi chef cooks right in front of you. You see every ingredient that goes into your meal. This transparency makes it easy to request modifications—less sauce, extra vegetables, specific protein preferences.

Your chef can accommodate nearly any request. Want extra vegetables instead of fried rice? More protein, less starch? Sauces on the side? Simply ask, and your meal can be customized to fit your nutritional goals.

Hibachi naturally provides balanced meals with protein, vegetables, and carbohydrates in one plate. The inclusion of fresh vegetables adds fiber, vitamins, and minerals without excessive calories.

"I was surprised how well hibachi fit into my diet. Fresh ingredients, visible cooking, reasonable portions. I can enjoy a delicious meal out and still meet my health goals."

— Verified Jinbeh Guest

Did You Know?

Hibachi grills reach temperatures of 400°F or higher — hot enough to sear protein in seconds with minimal added oils. This high-heat cooking method actually preserves more nutrients than boiling or steaming.

Source: Japanese Culinary Institute

The protein you choose is the foundation of your hibachi meal. Here's what you need to know about popular options:

Per serving, approximate values. Excludes sides and sauces.

Calories: 250-300 per serving Protein: 40-45g Fat: 8-10g

Chicken is an excellent choice for those watching calories. It's lean protein that's versatile and pairs well with vegetables. The light seasoning typical of hibachi preparation lets the natural flavor shine without excess calories. A typical serving includes grilled chicken, vegetables, and minimal added oil.

Best for: Calorie-conscious diners, those prioritizing protein

Calories: 150-200 per serving Protein: 20-25g Fat: 2-3g

Shrimp is the lowest-calorie hibachi protein at Jinbeh. It's naturally low in fat and calories while providing excellent protein. Beyond calories, shrimp offers significant nutritional benefits: it's rich in iodine (essential for thyroid function), contains omega-3 fatty acids (beneficial for heart health), and provides selenium and other minerals.

Best for: Lowest-calorie option, heart health, those prioritizing lean protein

The leanest protein on Jinbeh's hibachi menu at just 150–200 calories. Guests describe it as 'perfectly cooked' with a sweet, natural flavor. Pair with extra vegetables and steamed rice for a 350-calorie complete meal.

Calories: 180-220 per serving Protein: 20-22g Fat: 3-4g

Scallops are another excellent low-calorie seafood choice. They have a delicate flavor and tender texture that requires minimal seasoning. Scallops are good sources of magnesium and potassium, important for cardiovascular health and healthy blood pressure.

Best for: Low-calorie seafood lovers, cardiovascular health

Calories: 350-400 per serving Protein: 40-45g Fat: 15-20g (mostly healthy unsaturated fats)

While slightly higher in calories than chicken or shrimp, salmon provides superior nutritional value. It's rich in omega-3 fatty acids (EPA and DHA), which support heart health, reduce inflammation, and support brain function. The fats in salmon are predominantly heart-healthy unsaturated fats.

Best for: Heart health, those seeking healthy fats, omega-3 benefits

Calories: 400-450 per serving Protein: 45-50g Fat: 20-25g

Steak is the highest-calorie protein option at Jinbeh, but it remains a valuable choice. Premium cuts like filet mignon are actually relatively lean for beef. Steak provides excellent protein, iron (crucial for energy and oxygen transport), B12 (for nervous system health), and zinc (important for immune function).

To reduce calories, choose leaner cuts like filet mignon over ribeye, and pair with vegetable-heavy sides instead of fried rice.

Best for: Iron intake, special occasions, those prioritizing protein and satiety

Your protein choice significantly impacts meal calories, but sides can make even bigger differences. Here's what you need to know:

Chef's Pro Tip

Calories: 330-390 per serving Carbs: 50-60g Fat: 12-15g

Fried rice is delicious but calorie-dense. The calories come from cooking oil and butter used in preparation. A typical serving of fried rice can nearly double the calorie count of a meal. If you love fried rice, enjoy it in moderation, or request a smaller portion.

Lower-calorie alternatives: Request steamed rice instead (about 150-200 calories), or load your plate with extra vegetables and lighter sides.

Calories: 150-200 per serving Carbs: 35-45g Fat: 0-1g

Steamed rice provides the satisfying carbohydrates of fried rice with significantly fewer calories. Most hibachi restaurants can prepare steamed rice upon request. It provides the same meal structure without the added cooking fats.

Calories: 50-70 per serving Fiber: 3-5g Vitamins & Minerals: Excellent

This is where to load up! Hibachi vegetables—zucchini, onions, mushrooms, broccoli, carrots—are incredibly low in calories while being high in fiber, vitamins, and minerals. Requesting extra vegetables is the best way to make a meal more filling and nutritious without adding significant calories.

Vegetables provide satiety (feeling full longer) through their fiber content, which aids digestion and helps prevent overeating.

Ginger Sauce: 20-30 calories per tablespoon Soy Sauce: 10-15 calories per tablespoon Creamy Sauces: 50-80 calories per tablespoon

Sauces add flavor but can quickly add calories. A few tablespoons of creamy sauce can add 100-200 calories to your meal. Solution? Request sauces on the side so you control how much you use. You'll still get the flavor enhancement without excess calories.

Ginger sauce and soy-based sauces are lighter choices than creamy options.

Hibachi chicken has about 250-300 calories per serving. It's lean protein with vegetables. The exact amount depends on portion size. Hibachi cooking uses less oil than other methods, so it's a healthy choice.

Shrimp is the leanest choice at 150-200 calories. It's low in fat, high in protein, and rich in omega-3s. Chicken is around 250-300 calories. Both pair well with extra vegetables to fill your plate.

Hibachi fried rice has about 330-390 calories. Ask for steamed rice instead to save calories. You can also load your plate with vegetable sides. We're happy to customize your meal for your dietary goals.

Absolutely! Choose shrimp or chicken, request extra vegetables, ask for lighter sauces, and pick steamed rice. Hibachi cooking uses minimal oil. It's a great choice for people watching their intake.

Yes! Our hibachi chef can customize your meal. Ask for extra vegetables, lighter sauces on the side, and steamed rice. Hibachi cooking uses high heat with minimal oil. Welcome to the table—we'll help you make choices that fit your goals.

Steak and seafood like salmon and scallops have the most protein. Shrimp is excellent protein with lower calories. Chicken is a good lean choice too. Tell your chef your goals—we customize every plate.

Hibachi can absolutely be keto-friendly! Skip the fried rice and steamed rice, request double vegetables instead, and choose a protein like steak, chicken, or shrimp. Ask for sauces on the side since some contain sugar. A hibachi steak with extra veggies and no rice is a delicious low-carb meal under 500 calories.

Join us for an unforgettable hibachi dinner and a show. Family-owned since 1988, serving North Texas with authentic Japanese cuisine and warm hospitality.

### Body content

Immerse yourself in the art of hibachi dining. From sizzling proteins to creative vegetarian options, explore why hibachi combines culinary excellence with unforgettable entertainment for every occasion.

Key Takeaway

Hibachi dining combines live chef performances (knife tricks, onion volcanoes, fire shows) with fresh grilled proteins and sides — all prepared at your table. Plan 90 minutes to 2 hours, make reservations for weekends, and come hungry for generous portions.

- Home
- Blog
- Hibachi Dining Experience
Flames leap two feet off a 550-degree grill. A chef flips a shrimp into the air, catches it in his hat, and the whole table erupts. This is hibachi—and it's unlike any other dinner you'll have this year.

Did You Know?

Jinbeh has been serving authentic hibachi and sushi in the DFW area since 1988 — that's over 38 years of perfecting the craft. The word 'hibachi' literally means 'fire bowl' in Japanese, though the American-style tableside cooking is technically called 'teppanyaki.'

Source: Jinbeh Japanese Restaurant, est. 1988

Hibachi dining is an immersive experience that combines the pleasures of gastronomy with the thrill of live performance. The interaction between the chef and the diners adds a personal touch that elevates the dining experience beyond the ordinary. The communal setting around the grill fosters a sense of camaraderie among diners, making it an ideal choice for group gatherings and special occasions. Wondering about nutrition? Check out our hibachi calories guide for mindful dining tips.

Hibachi dining is more than just a meal—it's an experience. In many hibachi restaurants, diners gather around large, flat-top grills where skilled chefs prepare and cook food right before their eyes. The chefs are not only culinary experts but also performers, dazzling guests with knife tricks, flaming onion volcanoes, and playful banter.

Step 1 Be Seated at the Grill

You're seated communally around a large teppanyaki grill with 7–8 guests. Your server takes drink orders while you settle in.

Step 2 Soup & Salad Course

A warm bowl of Jinbeh's Japanese onion soup arrives, followed by a crisp house salad with house-made ginger dressing.

Step 3 The Chef Arrives

Your hibachi chef fires up the 400°F teppan grill and begins the show — spatula juggling, egg tricks, and the famous Beating Heart.

Step 4 The Onion Volcano

Stacked onion rings erupt in a dramatic flame — the crowd-favorite moment. Kids and adults alike cheer every time.

Step 5 Fried Rice & Vegetables

Your chef prepares fried rice with egg and grilled vegetables (zucchini, onions, mushrooms) in house-made garlic butter — pre-made the day before for maximum flavor.

Step 6 Protein Perfection

Your chosen protein is cooked to order: filet mignon, jumbo shrimp, chicken teriyaki, salmon, or one of our famous combos like Steak & Shrimp.

Step 7 The Shrimp Toss

The grand finale — your chef tosses shrimp through the air for you to catch in your mouth. A signature Jinbeh moment!

Step 8 Enjoy & Dessert

Dig into your perfectly plated meal with house-made yum yum sauce and dipping sauces. Save room for dessert!

Our signature yum yum sauce and spicy chili sauce — made in-house daily from family recipes

This interactive dining style is perfect for groups and celebrations, offering both delicious food and memorable entertainment. For larger parties, Jinbeh's private dining options provide a dedicated space with personalized service. It's a place where food meets art, and every dish tells a story that unfolds in real time.

The atmosphere in a hibachi restaurant is electric, filled with the sizzling sounds of cooking and the laughter of diners enjoying the show. The chefs, with their practiced hands and quick wit, engage the audience, making each meal a unique event. Watching them juggle utensils and create flaming spectacles adds an element of surprise and delight to the dining experience. This blend of culinary craftsmanship and theatrical flair is what sets hibachi apart from other dining options, making it an unforgettable outing for people of all ages.

When you sit down at a hibachi restaurant, you'll typically be presented with a diverse menu featuring a variety of meats, seafood, and vegetables. While the exact offerings can vary from one hibachi grill to another, there are some common elements you can expect to find. The menu is designed to cater to a wide range of tastes and dietary preferences, ensuring that everyone can find something they love.

From traditional Japanese flavors to innovative fusion dishes, hibachi menus offer a culinary journey that is both satisfying and adventurous. The diversity of the menu reflects the creativity and skill of hibachi chefs, who use fresh, high-quality ingredients to craft delicious meals. Each dish is prepared with precision and care, ensuring that the flavors are perfectly balanced and the presentation is visually appealing.

Most hibachi menus feature a selection of classic entrees such as chicken, steak, shrimp, and salmon. These proteins are often marinated and grilled to perfection, offering a savory and satisfying taste. If you're visiting a hibachi steakhouse, you might also find premium options like filet mignon or lobster tail. These dishes are typically accompanied by a side of fried rice, noodles, or vegetables, creating a well-rounded meal that is both delicious and fulfilling.

The classic hibachi entrees are beloved for their simplicity and the way they highlight the natural flavors of the ingredients. The grilling technique used in hibachi cooking imparts a smoky, charred flavor that enhances the taste of the meat or seafood. The chefs' skillful handling of the grill ensures that each entree is cooked to perfection, with a tender, juicy interior and a crisp, flavorful exterior.

Whether you prefer the rich taste of beef or the delicate sweetness of seafood, the classic hibachi entrees at Jinbeh offer something for everyone to enjoy. Visit our Frisco location or Lewisville location to experience our award-winning preparation techniques. Don't miss our hibachi vs teppanyaki guide to understand your dining experience.

Insider Tip

For those seeking meatless choices, many hibachi restaurant menus offer vibrant veggie hibachi options. These dishes often include a medley of fresh vegetables like zucchini, mushrooms, and bell peppers, all expertly seasoned and grilled. Some hibachi restaurants also offer tofu or vegetable-based options as part of their menu. These vegetarian options provide a flavorful and satisfying alternative to meat-based dishes, ensuring that vegetarians and vegans can enjoy the hibachi experience without compromise.

Vegetarian hibachi dishes are not only healthy but also bursting with flavor, thanks to the skillful use of seasonings and sauces. The combination of different vegetables creates a delightful array of textures and tastes, making each bite a culinary delight. The inclusion of tofu and other plant-based proteins adds a satisfying element to the meal, making it a complete and nourishing dining option.

Whether you're a dedicated vegetarian or simply looking to incorporate more plant-based meals into your diet, the vegetarian options on a hibachi menu are sure to please. At Jinbeh, our vegetarian hibachi preparations showcase the same culinary artistry and entertainment value as our meat dishes.

If you're having trouble deciding, consider trying a combination platter. These dishes allow you to enjoy multiple proteins in one meal, such as chicken and shrimp or steak and scallops. It's an excellent way to sample different flavors and textures without having to choose just one. Combination platters are a popular choice for those who want to experience the full range of hibachi offerings in a single sitting.

The beauty of combination platters lies in their versatility and the opportunity they provide to explore different culinary pairings. Each component of the platter is cooked to perfection, allowing you to savor the unique characteristics of each protein. The contrasting flavors and textures create a dynamic dining experience that keeps your taste buds engaged and excited.

When planning a hibachi outing, understanding the pricing can help you make informed choices. Hibachi prices can vary depending on the restaurant's location, the quality of ingredients, and the complexity of the dishes. Being aware of these factors can help you plan a dining experience that fits your budget while still allowing you to enjoy the full hibachi experience.

Type of Protein: Premium proteins like lobster or filet mignon will typically cost more than chicken or vegetables. The choice of protein is one of the main determinants of the overall cost of your meal.

Portion Size: Some restaurants offer larger portion sizes or additional sides for an extra fee. If you're dining with a larger group or have a hearty appetite, opting for a larger portion can be a good value.

Dining Experience: The entertainment aspect of hibachi dining may also impact the price, as you're paying for both the meal and the show. The skill and reputation of the chefs, as well as the overall ambiance of the restaurant, can influence the cost of your dining experience.

To find the best value, consider visiting during lunch hours when many hibachi restaurants offer discounted menus. Browse our lunch specials at our Frisco location — the same high-quality ingredients and expert preparation as dinner entrees, but at a reduced price. Or stop by during happy hour for special pricing on drinks to complement your meal. Check our full menu for all options.

Additionally, checking for local promotions or specials at your favorite hibachi restaurant can help you enjoy a delicious meal without breaking the bank. Some restaurants offer loyalty programs or special discounts for frequent diners, providing additional savings for those who love hibachi. Need midday inspiration? Browse our hibachi lunch ideas for affordable options.

Exploring hibachi menus during special events or holidays can also yield great deals and unique menu offerings. Many hibachi restaurants create themed dishes or offer special promotions to celebrate occasions, making it a perfect time to indulge in a hibachi feast. By staying informed about these opportunities, you can enjoy the rich flavors and exciting performances of hibachi dining at a price that feels just right.

When it comes to hibachi dining in North Texas, Jinbeh Japanese Restaurant stands out as a premier destination. With locations in both Frisco and Lewisville , Jinbeh has been serving families and celebrations since 1988. Our commitment to authentic Japanese cuisine, skilled chefs, and creating memorable experiences makes us a favorite among hibachi enthusiasts. Beyond hibachi, explore our sushi varieties and sushi for beginners options.

Signature Steaks: Jinbeh offers a range of steak options, including tender filet mignon and juicy ribeye. These cuts are expertly grilled to enhance their natural flavors and provide a melt-in-your-mouth experience.

Seafood Delights: From succulent shrimp to buttery scallops, seafood lovers will find plenty to enjoy. Our seafood dishes are prepared with the freshest ingredients, ensuring a taste that is both rich and refreshing.

Customizable Combos: Create your perfect meal by mixing and matching proteins and sides. Our customizable options allow you to tailor your meal to your preferences, ensuring a satisfying dining experience for everyone.

For those who prefer to enjoy hibachi at home, many restaurants offer hibachi takeout menus. These options allow you to experience the flavors of hibachi dining without the need to dine in. Simply call ahead or order online from your favorite hibachi restaurant, and enjoy the convenience of takeout or delivery.

The takeout experience offers the same high-quality ingredients and skillful preparation as dining in, ensuring that you don't miss out on the flavor and satisfaction that hibachi meals provide. Many restaurants offer special packaging to keep the food hot and fresh, allowing you to enjoy your meal at its best.

When searching for a hibachi restaurant, consider the following tips to ensure a fantastic dining experience:

Read Reviews: Check online reviews to see what other diners have to say about the food and entertainment. Reviews can provide valuable insights into the quality of the food, the skill of the chefs, and the overall dining experience.

Check the Menu: Look for a diverse menu that offers options for all dietary preferences. A varied menu ensures that everyone in your party can find something they enjoy, from meat lovers to vegetarians.

Consider the Atmosphere: Whether you're planning a family outing or a romantic date, choose a restaurant with an ambiance that suits your occasion. The right setting can enhance the dining experience, making it more enjoyable and memorable.

Make Reservations: For the best experience, especially for groups, making reservations ensures you get seated together at the same grill. This is crucial for enjoying the full hibachi experience.

Exploring the delights of hibachi menus is a journey filled with flavor, fun, and unforgettable memories. Whether dining in or taking out, the vibrant offerings of hibachi grills provide something for everyone. From classic steak and seafood dishes to creative vegetarian delights, there's a world of taste waiting at your nearest hibachi grill.

The magic of hibachi lies in its ability to transform a meal into an event, offering a unique blend of culinary art and entertainment. As you delve into the diverse and exciting world of hibachi dining, you'll discover new flavors, meet skilled chefs, and create memories that will last a lifetime.

Whether you're celebrating a special occasion or simply enjoying a night out, hibachi dining offers an experience that is as delightful as it is delicious. To create a delicious hibachi lunch, you'll need a few key ingredients:

- Protein: Chicken, beef, shrimp, or tofu, each offering a different texture and flavor profile to suit your taste.
- Vegetables: Bell peppers, onions, zucchini, and mushrooms, chosen for their ability to absorb flavors and provide a satisfying crunch.
- Rice: Preferably short-grain or jasmine rice, which offers the perfect base for soaking up sauces and flavors.
- Sauces: Soy sauce, teriyaki sauce, and sesame oil for flavor, providing a savory and aromatic touch to the meal.
- Seasonings: Garlic, ginger, and sesame seeds, essential for adding depth and complexity to the dish.
Prepare the Rice: Cook your rice according to package instructions. For added flavor, you can stir in a bit of sesame oil once it's cooked, ensuring each grain is infused with a rich, nutty aroma.

Sauté the Vegetables: Heat a pan or flat griddle over medium-high heat. Add a splash of sesame oil, then sauté your choice of vegetables until they are tender-crisp. This quick cooking method ensures the vegetables retain their vibrant colors and natural sweetness.

Cook the Protein: In the same pan, add your choice of protein. Season with soy sauce, garlic, and ginger, and cook until the protein is thoroughly cooked and slightly caramelized. This step is crucial for developing the rich, umami flavors characteristic of hibachi cooking.

Combine and Serve: Mix the cooked vegetables and protein with the rice. Garnish with sesame seeds and serve with your favorite dipping sauce, adding an extra layer of flavor to the dish. This simple yet effective combination offers a homemade hibachi experience that rivals any restaurant offering.

Navigate the world of hibachi dining with our comprehensive menu guide. From appetizers to desserts, discover what makes hibachi dining special and how to find the perfect dish for your palate.

Key Takeaway

A hibachi menu features sizzling proteins (steak, chicken, shrimp, lobster), fried rice, grilled vegetables, and interactive chef entertainment — all prepared fresh at your table. Most meals include soup, salad, appetizer, entrée, and dessert for a complete dining experience.

- Home
- Blog
- Hibachi Menu Guide
Your server drops the menu and you freeze. Filet mignon or the combo? Yum Yum sauce or garlic butter? Add the lobster tail? At a hibachi restaurant, every choice shapes the experience—and knowing the menu before you sit down means you order like a regular, not a rookie.

Every sauce at Jinbeh is made from scratch. The famous Yum Yum sauce is an in-house mayo-based blend with sriracha and sugar — people are genuinely addicted to it. The Blaster sauce is Jinbeh's “spicy” option (honestly not that spicy — even cautious diners handle it fine). For the truly brave, there's a secret sriracha-togarashi paste. And ponzu ? House-made, lemony, and perfect with tataki dishes.

The Hidden Vegetables: Jinbeh's fried rice contains finely chopped scallion, onion, and carrots—but they're cut so small you can't see them. This is deliberate: early feedback told the kitchen there were too many visible vegetables. Now the chopping is so fine it's invisible. The result? Kids happily eat their veggies without knowing it.

The Sauces (All Handmade): Yum Yum sauce is a mayo-based blend with sriracha and sugar that guests call “addictive.” The Blaster sauce is Jinbeh's “spicy” option, but honestly? Even non-spicy customers handle it fine. For true heat seekers, the kitchen keeps a house sriracha-togarashi paste. Every sauce recipe is typed out and hung on the kitchen walls—every cook learns them.

The Grill: Hibachi grills reach approximately 550°F. At that temperature, cross-contamination from allergens is extremely difficult. Gluten-free is easy: only the sauces contain gluten, not the base ingredients. Every grill is cleaned after each use and the restaurant is deep cleaned twice daily.

Hibachi is a style of Japanese cooking that involves grilling food on a high-heat metal plate. The origins of hibachi can be traced back to ancient Japan, where it was primarily used as a heating device before evolving into a cooking method. In America, hibachi is often associated with teppanyaki—learn more about the hibachi vs teppanyaki differences . Chefs perform cooking tricks and engage with diners around a communal grill. This interactive dining style not only highlights the chefs' culinary skills but also creates a lively atmosphere that enhances the dining experience.

Did You Know?

The hibachi/teppanyaki restaurant industry in the United States is worth over $4.2 billion annually, with more than 4,000 locations nationwide. The interactive dining format was popularized in the US by Benihana in 1964 — but family-owned restaurants like Jinbeh (est. 1988) are where locals find the most authentic experience, personalized service, and highest-quality ingredients.

Source: IBISWorld & National Restaurant Association

Step 1 Start with Appetizers

Browse gyoza, edamame, and tempura. At Jinbeh, guests rave about the crab rangoons — freshly made and packed with real crab meat.

Step 2 Choose Your Protein

Pick from filet mignon, NY strip, chicken teriyaki, shrimp, scallops, or lobster tail. Combos like Steak & Shrimp are fan favorites.

Step 3 Don't Skip the Fried Rice

Multiple reviewers call Jinbeh's fried rice the best they've ever had. It's prepared on the grill with house-made garlic butter — a must-order.

Step 4 Add Sauces & Drinks

Try the mustard dipping sauce (guests call it 'excellent') alongside ginger and yum-yum sauce. Pair with Sapporo on tap or a lychee martini.

Step 5 Finish with Dessert

End with ice cream tempura — warm, crispy batter around cold ice cream. Reviewers say it's 'visually appealing and delicious.'

A typical hibachi menu offers a variety of meats, seafood, and vegetables. The selection is designed to cater to a wide range of tastes and preferences, allowing diners to customize their meal to their liking. Guests can choose from options like steak, chicken, shrimp, and scallops, often accompanied by a range of vegetables such as zucchini, onions, and mushrooms. These ingredients are typically fresh and locally sourced, ensuring the highest quality and flavor.

The meals are typically served with fried rice or noodles and a selection of dipping sauces, each contributing a unique taste profile that complements the main dish. This combination of elements creates a balanced meal that satisfies both the palate and the appetite.

Hibachi menus often begin with a selection of appetizers. These starters are designed to whet your appetite and set the tone for the main course. Common starters include edamame, gyoza (Japanese dumplings), and tempura vegetables or shrimp.

Edamame: Lightly salted and steamed, edamame offers a healthy and refreshing start. These young soybeans are perfect for sharing and provide a satisfying bite.

Gyoza: Japanese dumplings with a tender filling and crispy exterior, gyoza provides a savory bite that awakens the palate. These are often served with a dipping sauce that enhances their flavor.

Tempura: With its light and airy batter, tempura showcases the delicate flavors of the vegetables or seafood within. These dishes are perfect for sharing, encouraging a communal dining experience and fostering conversation among diners. They set the stage for the main event, creating anticipation for the flavors to come.

The star of any hibachi menu is undoubtedly the main course. These dishes are carefully crafted to highlight the natural flavors of the ingredients while incorporating the distinct taste of the hibachi grill.

Steak: A classic choice at any hibachi steakhouse, diners can select from a variety of cuts, each offering a unique texture and flavor profile. Whether you prefer a tender filet mignon or a flavorful sirloin, the meat is cooked to your liking and often paired with garlic butter for added richness. The high heat of the hibachi grill sears the meat, locking in juices and creating a delicious crust.

Seafood: Seafood lovers will find plenty to enjoy, with offerings like shrimp, scallops, and lobster tail. The fresh seafood is a highlight of the hibachi menu, celebrated for its delicate and sweet flavors. These dishes are typically seasoned with soy sauce and lemon, enhancing the natural flavors of the seafood and adding a hint of umami.

Chicken: For those who prefer poultry, hibachi chicken is a popular option. The chicken is marinated in teriyaki sauce, imparting a sweet and savory taste that is both comforting and satisfying. Cooked to perfection on the hibachi grill, the chicken remains moist and flavorful. At Jinbeh, our chicken is sourced fresh and prepared with expert precision .

Premium Options: Pork and lamb might also be available, depending on the restaurant, offering additional options for meat lovers. These meats are often seasoned with a blend of spices and sauces, creating a unique flavor profile that complements the main ingredients.

No hibachi meal is complete without the sides. These accompaniments are essential to the hibachi experience, providing balance and variety to the meal. Fried rice and noodles are staples, each cooked with a mix of eggs, vegetables, and soy sauce. The rice is typically fluffy and flavorful, absorbing the sauces and juices from the main dishes.

Fried Rice: Often cooked right before your eyes on the grill, fried rice is seasoned to perfection and incorporates fresh vegetables for nutritional balance and visual appeal.

House-made with garlic butter, egg, and fresh vegetables on the teppan grill. Guests consistently call it 'the best fried rice I've ever had' — and it's a must-add to any hibachi order.

Noodles: Chewy and satisfying, noodles offer a delightful texture and are often stir-fried with similar ingredients to the rice, creating a harmonious blend of flavors.

Grilled Vegetables: Zucchini, onions, mushrooms, and broccoli are grilled alongside the main dishes, providing a healthy and delicious accompaniment. The charred edges and tender centers of the vegetables add depth and complexity to the meal.

Hibachi meals are often accompanied by a variety of sauces, including ginger, mustard, and yum-yum sauce. These condiments are an integral part of the hibachi dining experience, allowing diners to customize the flavor of their meal.

- Ginger Sauce: Offers a refreshing and tangy taste
- Mustard Sauce: Adds a spicy kick to your meal
- Yum-Yum Sauce: A creamy and slightly sweet condiment that is versatile and rich in flavor
- Soy Sauce: The classic pairing for any hibachi dish
These sauces add a personal touch to each bite, enhancing the overall dining experience and allowing diners to experiment with different flavor combinations.

After enjoying the savory delights of a hibachi meal, dessert is a must. A sweet ending provides a satisfying conclusion to the dining experience, cleansing the palate and leaving a lasting impression.

Mochi Ice Cream: With its chewy rice cake exterior and creamy interior, mochi ice cream offers a unique texture and taste that delights the senses.

Tempura-Fried Bananas: Warm and crispy, tempura-fried bananas provide a delightful contrast to cool desserts.

Green Tea Ice Cream: Prized for its subtle and earthy flavor, green tea ice cream provides a refreshing end to the meal, ensuring you leave with a smile.

Prices at hibachi restaurants can vary based on location and the choice of ingredients. The experience is often considered a special occasion, with the prices reflecting the quality of the ingredients and the skill of the chefs. For instance, a hibachi steakhouse menu might have higher prices due to premium cuts of meat. However, most establishments offer a range of options to suit different budgets, ensuring the hibachi experience is accessible to all.

Lunch Specials: Many hibachi restaurants offer lunch specials, providing a more affordable way to enjoy the experience. These specials typically include a smaller portion of the main dishes, allowing you to savor the flavors at a reduced price. Jinbeh's lunch specials are among the most affordable in the area.

Shared Meals: Consider sharing entrees or opting for combination meals that allow you to try multiple items at a reduced price. Sharing not only makes the meal more affordable but also adds to the communal aspect of the dining experience, encouraging conversation and bonding over food.

For those who prefer dining at home, many hibachi restaurants offer takeout menus. This option allows you to enjoy the flavors and excitement of hibachi without leaving the comfort of your home. These menus often include the same selections as dine-in options, allowing you to enjoy the flavors of hibachi in your own space.

The convenience of takeout means you can enjoy a hibachi meal on your own schedule, making it a perfect choice for busy weeknights or relaxed weekends. To ensure the best takeout experience:

- Check Availability: Not all dishes may be available for takeout, so it's wise to check the menu ahead of time.
- Plan for Cooking Time: Hibachi dishes are best enjoyed fresh, so plan your pickup time accordingly to ensure the best experience.
- Order Online: Many restaurants offer online ordering for convenience, allowing you to skip the line.
While hibachi is a highlight, Japanese steakhouses often offer other dining options. These establishments celebrate the rich culinary traditions of Japan, providing a diverse range of dishes that go beyond the hibachi grill. Sushi and sashimi , and traditional Japanese dishes like ramen or udon are commonly available, providing a wider range of flavors and experiences.

Whether you're in the mood for the delicate taste of raw fish or the comforting warmth of a noodle soup, these options ensure there's something for everyone to enjoy.

Known for its high-quality ingredients and skilled chefs, Jinbeh is a favorite among hibachi enthusiasts looking for an exceptional dining experience.

Highlights from Jinbeh's menu include signature steaks with expert grilling, fresh seafood selections, customizable combinations, and a commitment to quality and innovation that makes it a standout choice for hibachi dining.

Kids get the same entertaining show as adults — the fire tricks and food-tossing are always a hit. Children's meals typically include smaller protein portions with rice and vegetables.

Join us for an unforgettable hibachi dinner and a show. Family-owned since 1988, serving North Texas with authentic Japanese cuisine and warm hospitality.
